notes:
PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); the package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null), and no hardware was attached or run.

WHAT IT SERVES: the card's models[0], mujoco_playground/_src/dm_control_suite/xmls/acrobot.xml, as a MujocoDriver in simulated mode R0. cap.world.step.v1 takes {ticks, action: {ctrl: [...]}}; each ctrl element is checked by the bridge against the model's actuator_ctrlrange before data.ctrl is written, then mj_step runs ticks times. cap.world.reset.v1 restores the model defaults with mj_resetData + mj_forward. The state is the bridge's integration state (time_ms, qpos, qvel, ctrl, tick, timestep_ms, seed). The other card models and environment classes are not served: one package serves one device, models[0]. The driver declares no Limit of its own; the only actuation bound is the model's elbow motor ctrlrange -1 to 1 (acrobot.xml:41), which the bridge derives at load time.

WHY THIS SHAPE: the card's helper is MujocoDriver (family-config), and the upstream environment class Balance loads this MJCF into mujoco.MjModel (acrobot.py:62-67). MuJoCo is not installed where the gate runs, so backends['fake'] is the package's stand-in mujoco module in fake.py (the form the SDK's own MujocoDriver tests use). The lock names it .fake:FakeMujoco. It parses the same MJCF text for the actuator count, the control range, the joint dimensions and the option timestep, but integrates a placeholder motion; the fidelity gaps list every difference. The class's native symbol is the card entry symbol acrobot:Balance for traceability, while the fake surface is the mujoco library the bridge consumes.

NOT COVERED: MuJoCo itself and the JAX/MJX environment were never imported, so no trajectory was compared with the real engine or with Balance; the upstream random reset, observation, tolerance reward and NaN episode logic are not exposed; the stand-in loads no mesh or texture, resolves no contact, constraint or tendon and does not apply the actuator gear ratio; no physical acrobot is modelled and nothing was validated against hardware.

WARNINGS (all expected, none failed): G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND because backends['fake'] is a package object standing in for the mujoco library rather than a package class the gate can wrap in a Recorder, and G8.NO_UNIT x3 for ticks, action.ctrl[*] and seed, the integer/numeric inputs the simulator family derives. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning was raised.

TESTS: test_driver.py keeps mhs.testing.check_driver and adds six cases (model shape from the card model, control-range refusals with zero effect, state following the control, reset to the model defaults, published fidelity contract, e-stop latch); they pass. No catalogue_requests: the package uses only cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1.
